sections.overview: The lesula is a guenon of the central Congo forests, described as a new species only in 2012. The first one noticed by scientists was a young pet in the town of Opala in 2007; fieldwork then found it living wild in a forest block that had hardly been explored. It is listed as Vulnerable.
sections.identification: A medium-sized, slim monkey. Measured adult males had a body of 47–65 cm and weighed 4.0–7.1 kg, but only a few animals were measured and no adult female was. It has a long grizzled blond mane, a black back banded with amber, and an amber patch brightest at the base of the tail. Throat and chest are yellowish buff, shoulders and limbs black, thighs silvery grey and the tail black beyond its amber base. The bare face is pale pinkish grey to tan with a cream stripe down the nose, and adult males have a bright blue scrotum and perineum.
sections.habitat: It lives in mature upland evergreen humid forest, including forests dominated by Gilbertiodendron, at 400–715 m. It was seen less often in regrowth near villages and never in seasonally flooded forest or savanna gallery forest. Its known range covers about 17,000 km² in central Congo, between the middle Lomami River in the east and the upper Tshuapa River in the west.
sections.diet: It eats leaf stalks, ripe and unripe fruit, flower buds and growing shoots of two ground-living herbs of the arrowroot family, and also picks up food dropped by other primates feeding above. The full diet and its seasonal changes have not been documented.
sections.behavior: It is semi-terrestrial: of 48 animals seen, about a third were on the ground when first met, and fleeing animals often ran along the ground. It was usually met alone or in groups of up to five, and in 11 of 19 encounters it was with other monkeys. At dawn, low booming calls given in bouts of two or three are heard over long distances; the callers were almost certainly males.
sections.reproduction: Almost nothing is documented about its breeding in the wild: season, gestation, litter and lifespan are all unknown. The only detail reported is that young are pale blond overall and that the amber patch on the back appears within their first three months.
sections.ecology: It often travels with other monkeys, such as Wolf’s mona monkey, the red-tailed monkey and the red colobus. The only recorded predation was one attack by a crowned eagle. Its ecological role has not been studied.
sections.conservation: It is listed as Vulnerable. The main threat is bushmeat hunting, which has grown over the past decade and feeds city markets such as Kindu and Kisangani; its range was not yet logged or mined when it was described. It was the least often seen primate in the surveys, though the authors called it not uncommon in its range. Population size has not been estimated, and a protected area of about 9,000 km² was proposed in 2012.
